questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Browser Performance”?
options: Browser Performance means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Browser Performance removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Browser Performance should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Browser Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Browser Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Browser Performance is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Avoiding forced layout work” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Avoiding forced layout work” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Avoiding forced layout work” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Avoiding forced layout work” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Avoiding forced layout work” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Avoiding forced layout work” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Avoiding forced layout work” under Browser Performance. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Browser Performance”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
